intent: Specify the public functions `quantiles::greenwald_khanna::find_insert_pos(vs: &[T], v: &T) -> usize` and `find_insert_pos_linear(vs: &[T], v: &T) -> usize`, instantiated at `T = i32`. In Lean they are `greenwald_khanna.find_insert_pos core.I32.Insts.CoreCmpOrd vs v` and `greenwald_khanna.find_insert_pos_linear core.I32.Insts.CoreCmpOrd vs v` with `vs : Slice Std.I32`, `v : Std.I32`.

manual_mutants.note: elements equal to the pivot send the search to the left half (wrong only when v equals the middle element)
manual_mutants.after: { corecmpOrdInst.PartialOrdInst with lt := corecmpOrdInst.PartialOrdInst.le } v pivot

manual_mutants.note: linear scan returns the lower bound (first element >= v) instead of the upper bound
manual_mutants.after: { corecmpOrdInst.PartialOrdInst with lt := corecmpOrdInst.PartialOrdInst.le } v vi

manual_mutants.note: right half starts after the pivot, but the offset is not adjusted (off by one for large slices)
manual_mutants.after: T) vs { start := (if middle.val + 1 ≤ i.val then ⟨middle.bv + 1⟩ else middle) }

manual_mutants.note: linear scan returns len - 1 when every element is <= v
manual_mutants.after: | core.option.Option.None => let i ← (do let n ← core.slice.Slice.len vs; if n = 0#usize then ok n else n - 1#usize)

manual_mutants.note: threshold for switching to the linear scan raised but the binary step compares with the element before the middle
manual_mutants.after: let pivot ← (do let m ← middle - 1#usize; Slice.index_usize vs m)
